audit.whatIsWrong: The poke is called a 'Q acceleration-gate' or 'Q gate' in `spikes[0]`, `early`, `wants.you[0]`, `wants.foe[0]` and `whys[0]` — one ability name built out of two different abilities.
audit.why: Acceleration Gate is Jayce's E in Cannon stance; Shock Blast is his Q in Cannon stance. They are separate casts: he drops the gate, then fires the bolt through it for bonus missile speed, range and damage. Collapsing them into 'Q gate' costs the player the single most useful tell in the lane — the gate lands first and visibly, which is advance warning that the empowered bolt is about to follow. A player told to watch one spell watches the wrong half of the sequence.
audit.corrected: Acceleration Gate (E) goes down first; Shock Blast (Q) is fired through it. The gate appearing is the cue to hold Rebuttal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mercury Cannon / Mercury Hammer is never mentioned in the content layer at all, even though the all-in is described three separate times.
audit.why: Riot's text: the first attack after swapping to Cannon 'reduces the target's Armor AND Magic Resist'. Mel is a pure magic-damage champion who builds no defences, so a Jayce who opens his all-in with the stance-swap auto is stripping the exact resistance her survival depends on before any damage lands. The swap is also an auto-attack reset on a 6s cooldown, which means the readable tell is an attack wind-up rather than a spell cast. Both facts are absent and both change how the all-in is read.
audit.corrected: Mercury Cannon's first attack shreds armour and MR and is an auto-reset on a 6s swap — that auto is the start of the combo, not the leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: `spikes[2]`, `whys[2]` and `whys[5]` call the hammer displacement 'hammer E-knockback' without naming it or noting what it does to Mel specifically.
audit.why: Thundering Blow is Hammer-stance E at 240 range and it knocks Mel back. Mel has no dash anywhere in her kit, so a displacement is not just repositioning — it is the one thing she cannot undo, and it sets the distance for everything that follows. Naming it and flagging the no-dash consequence is worth more than the generic 'burst combo' phrasing.
audit.corrected: Thundering Blow (Hammer E) knocks you back and you have no dash to reset the spacing.

audit.whatIsWrong: full `breakdown.cooldowns` says to 'read it like a second minimap' but gives no number for Shock Blast, and never mentions the 6s stance swap.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 falling to 6s. Mercury Cannon/Hammer swaps on a flat 6s. Those two numbers together define the rhythm of the lane: early on there is a real 16-second gap between empowered pokes, and the stance clock tells you whether he is set up to poke or to all-in right now.
audit.corrected: Shock Blast 16s at rank 1 down to 6s; stance swap is a flat 6s.

audit.why: 42.86% over 14 games, carried consistently. No elo-tier language anywhere in the entry.

The win condition on disk is right and is the reason this entry is in better shape than most: Jayce falls off, Mel's Overwhelm scales without a cap, and Golden Eclipse is a 25000-range detonation that does not require her to re-enter his poke range. `late` and `spikes[3]` both state this correctly and were left alone.

notes: Two things left deliberately untouched. (1) `wants.you[0]` says Rebuttal fires his poke back 'as magic damage'. Shock Blast is flagged projectile so the reflect itself is sound, but nothing in the kit files establishes the damage type of a reflected projectile, so I removed the reflect line's damage-type claim rather than restate it. (2) The content chart gives Jayce 5 of 7 stages against a 42.86% win rate, which is internally consistent, but the full layer grades the same matchup EVEN 5.5/10 with Skill across all seven phases. The two layers disagree; I did not force a reconciliation because either reading is defensible at 42.86% and inventing a power shift to settle it would be worse than leaving the disagreement visible. Worth a human decision.

edits.after: Acceleration Gate (E) then Shock Blast (Q) fired through it out-ranges you — he chunks you off CS before Q+E come online.

edits.after: Mercury Cannon's first hit shreds your armour and MR, then Thundering Blow knocks you back into the combo — his hardest all-in.

edits.before: Jayce out-pokes you outright in the first three levels and that is the honest truth — his accelerated Q gate hits harder and from farther than your single Q bolt, and he can do it before you've got Solar Snare or Rebuttal up to answer. Your one tool is W: time the barrier to eat his cannon Q and spit it back, but he can bait that. Don't walk up to throw a Q he'll just gate-poke you for — last-hit at max range, hold E for when he commits to cannon range, and accept you're behind.
edits.after: Jayce out-pokes you outright in the first three levels and that is the honest truth — a Shock Blast fired through his own Acceleration Gate gains missile speed, range and damage, and he does it before you have Solar Snare or Rebuttal to answer. The gate is your tell: once it drops, the empowered bolt is coming through it, so hold Rebuttal for that one and let the ungated bolts go. Don't walk up to throw a Q he'll gate-poke you for — last-hit at max range, hold E for when he commits to cannon range.

edits.before: This stays his lane through levels 4-5 — his Q poke keeps you below the Overwhelm thresholds you need and you can't trade back without eating his hammer combo. At 6 you get your one swing: if you can land Solar Snare's root, Golden Eclipse detonates whatever stacks you built for a real burst from range, which is the moment he respects you. But it's a coin-flip window, not a takeover — if you miss the root, he gates in with hammer E-knockback and the cannon combo and you die. Bait his all-in onto your W wall, then R.
edits.after: This stays his lane through levels 4-5 — his Shock Blast keeps you below the Overwhelm thresholds you need and you can't trade back without eating the hammer combo. Know what starts it: Mercury Cannon is a 6s stance swap whose first attack strips your armour and magic resist before anything else lands, so that auto is the tell, not the leap. At 6 you get your one swing: land Solar Snare's root and Golden Eclipse detonates whatever stacks you built, from range. Miss it and Thundering Blow knocks you into the combo instead.
